exercise.name: Step-up

reference.title: Step-up (female)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

exercise.laterality: Unilateral (lead leg works up and down)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you drive up onto the box, inhale as you step down.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, short stand on top, about 1.5 s down with the lead leg controlling

prescription.tempo: Up in about 1 s, down in 1.5-2 s
prescription.progression: Higher box (up to knee height), then hold dumbbells

cues.text: Stand tall facing the box, hands on hips.
Place the whole right foot on the box, knee over the middle of the foot.
Breathe out and drive through the right heel to stand up; let the left foot follow without pushing hard off the floor.
Stand tall on the box, hips and knees straight.
Breathe in and step the left foot down behind you slowly; the right leg does the lowering.
Bring the right foot down beside the left.
Reset and repeat on the same leg, then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Pushing off the floor with the back foot
mistakes.fix: Keep the back foot light; the lead leg does the work.
Keep the knee over the 2nd-3rd toe.

mistakes.mistake: Only the toes on the box
mistakes.fix: Place the whole foot so the heel can take the weight.
Lower under control; the lead leg bends to let the back foot reach the floor.

kinematics.norm: Commonly 15-45 cm; studies used 15 cm (MacAskill 2014) and 45.7 cm (Simenz 2010)
About 120 degrees at foot contact on a 40.6 cm step, about 90 degrees on a 20.3 cm step (Smutnick 2009)
About 92 degrees on a 40.6 cm step, about 66 degrees on a 20.3 cm step (Smutnick 2009)
Bends until the back foot reaches the floor (clinical opinion)
Slight forward lean over the lead foot (clinical opinion)
About 2 s per step-up was used in MacAskill 2014; controlled lowering (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Smutnick & Bohannon 2009, hip and knee flexion of lead and trail limbs during ascent of a step of different heights by normal adults (Physiotherapy 95(4))
MacAskill, Durant & Wallace 2014, gluteal muscle activity during weightbearing and non-weightbearing exercise (Int J Sports Phys Ther 9(7):907-914; PMC4275195)
Simenz, Garceau, Lutsch, Suchomel & Ebben 2010, electromyographical analysis of lower extremity muscle activation during variations of the loaded step up exercise (ISBS 2010 proceedings)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Use a stable box that cannot slide or tip.
modify: Knee pain: use a lower box (15-20 cm) so the knee bends less.
Balance concerns: hold a wall or rail with one hand.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Lead-leg knee extensors drive the body up onto the box and control the step down. The lead knee starts deeply bent on a 40 cm box (about 120 degrees at 40.6 cm in Smutnick 2009).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Lead-leg knee extensors drive the body up onto the box and control the step down. The lead knee starts deeply bent on a 40 cm box (about 120 degrees at 40.6 cm in Smutnick 2009).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Lead-leg hip extensor, working hardest at the start of the drive while the hip is flexed. Unloaded step-ups on a 6-inch step gave only about 30% MVIC (MacAskill 2014); a higher box or added load asks more of it.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Lead-leg hip extensor, working hardest at the start of the drive while the hip is flexed. Unloaded step-ups on a 6-inch step gave only about 30% MVIC (MacAskill 2014); a higher box or added load asks more of it.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension from the deep start position.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension from the deep start position.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and steady the knee.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and steady the knee.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the lead shin on the box; the trailing calf gives a small push-off from the floor.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the lead shin on the box; the trailing calf gives a small push-off from the floor.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on one leg. In unloaded forward step-ups it was more active than gluteus maximus, about 63% MVIC (MacAskill 2014).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level on one leg. In unloaded forward step-ups it was more active than gluteus maximus, about 63% MVIC (MacAskill 2014).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall and the pelvis level while one foot is in the air.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk upright as it leans slightly forward over the lead foot.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk upright as it leans slightly forward over the lead foot.

guides.label: Hips rise up and forward over the box foot
